key_insight: LeVo 2 combines hierarchical representation modeling with progressive post-training to generate full-length songs that are both structurally coherent and acoustically rich. It aims to keep vocals, accompaniment, lyrics, and prompts aligned without sacrificing global song planning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of generating complete songs that remain coherent over long spans while preserving track-level acoustic detail. It tackles the trade-off between mixed-token models, which keep vocal-instrument coordination but blur details, and dual-track models, which improve acoustics but increase sequence length and weaken global planning.
method: Uses a hybrid LLM-Diffusion framework for controllable full-length song generation.
Applies hierarchical representation modeling to better separate and preserve song structure and track-specific details.
Uses progressive post-training to improve stability, musicality, and alignment with lyrics/prompts over long outputs.
impact: This matters because it moves AI music generation closer to usable, end-to-end song creation with better long-range coherence and sound quality. Practitioners working on generative audio can use this direction to balance controllability, fidelity, and scalability more effectively.

paper_title: LeVo 2: Stable and Melodious Song Generation via Hierarchical Representation Modeling and Progressive Post-Training
paper_authors: Shun Lei, Huaicheng Zhang, Dapeng Wu, Yaoxun Xu, Lishi Zuo
